use deepseek api to run api call 

```{python}
## VERYFYING THE KEY EXISTS AND CAN BE USED 
import os 
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI

load_dotenv(override=True)

deepseek_api_key = os.getenv("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY")

if not deepseek_api_key: 
  print("There is no deepseek api key in your evn")
elif not deepseek_api_key.startswith("sk-"):
  print("The doesn't start with sk-")
else: 
  print("Your DEEPSEEK API KEY is ready to use. ENJOY")

```


```{python}
"""
from aiohttp import client
We can create two lines, 
one is client calling api that contains the base url and the api key 
the other one is response that contains the model and the message 
"""

DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL = "https://api.deepseek.com"
deepseek = OpenAI(base_url = DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL, api_key = deepseek_api_key) 
DEEPSEEK_MODEL = "deepseek-flash"

response = deepseek.chat.completions.create(model = DEEPSEEK_MODEL, messages=[
  {"role":"user", "content": "Tell me a fun fact about China that few know about it"}
])
response.choices[0].message.content
```

```{python}


## Import all the needed packages 
## get the api key 
## verify the api key 

import os 
from dotenv import load_dotenv 
from openai import OpenAI

openrouter_api_key = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")

if not openrouter_api_key: 
  print("There is no openrouter api key in env")
elif not openrouter_api_key.startswith("sk-or-v1"):
  print("the key is not the right key")
else: 
  print("The Openrouter Api Key exists and read to use. ")

```



Establishing the api call requires two thhings: Client and Response 
Client requires api key and baseline url 
Response requires client and content 

```{python}

OPENROUTER_BASE_URL ="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

openrouter = OpenAI(api_key=openrouter_api_key, base_url=OPENROUTER_BASE_URL)

response = openrouter.chat.completions.create(model = "openrouter/free", messages=[
  {"role": "user", "content":  "Tell me a fun fact!"}
])

response.choices[0].message.content
```

checking what model open router gives me all the time 


```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
display(Markdown(response.choices[0].message.content))


```


```{python}
import json
response.model
response.usage

print(f"Model Used: {response.model}")
print(f"Finish Reason: {response.choices[0].finish_reason}")
print(f"Total Tokens Used: {response.usage.total_tokens}")
print(f"AI Content:\n{response.choices[0].message.content}")
response.json()

```


again, each api call has two components: Clients and Response 
Clients consists of two components, base url and api key 
response consists of model and messages and messages itself consists of two additiional components user and content
